submission.justification: Recommend Absorber-F1 with 4.5 mm plates. Project documents list Absorber-F1 as an allowed candidate absorber, note that all candidates can be machined to required tolerances, and state that the support/readout/cooling interfaces are common or compatible across candidates. The 2025 reference at 5 mm already showed F1 as the best material among the candidates (F1 3.2%, F3 3.9%, F2 5.1% at 100 GeV). I then scanned the allowed 2–10 mm range with the current simulation. F1 remained clearly superior to F2 and F3; for F1, repeated simulations around the minimum gave the best observed average performance at 4.5 mm, about 3.17% energy resolution at 100 GeV. Nearby tested F1 settings were slightly worse on average: 4.25 mm about 3.21%, 5.0 mm about 3.20%, and 6.0 mm about 3.23%, while thicker plates degraded further. Therefore 4.5 mm F1 is the best resolution choice found within the allowed design space.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV.
requirements.evidence: Current simulation scan found Absorber-F1 to be the best material; repeated runs around the optimum gave about 3.17% at 4.5 mm, better than nearby F1 thicknesses tested and clearly better than F3 (~3.8–4.0% near its best tested region) and F2 (>5%). The 2025 5 mm comparison also ranked F1 best: F1 3.2%, F3 3.9%, F2 5.1%.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Absorber-F1, Absorber-F2, and Absorber-F3 as candidate absorber materials; the recommendation selects Absorber-F1.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns.
requirements.evidence: No project document identifies a material-specific maintenance exclusion for Absorber-F1. The meeting notes state the mechanical support is compatible with every candidate absorber, readout.md states the silicon-pad readout and front-end ASIC are common to all absorber options, and cooling.md states the common water-cooling concept with heat load dominated by front-end electronics. Thus the selected absorber does not introduce a documented obstacle to the shutdown maintenance concept.
The recommended plate thickness is 4.5 mm, within the allowed 2–10 mm interval.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended material and plate thickness.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Absorber-F1 with 4.5 mm plates.
